# Relevo

> Relevo is a durable task execution engine built with Python and PostgreSQL. Applications submit background jobs; independent workers execute registered handlers, while a coordinator and recovery scheduler track ownership and recover interrupted attempts. It is a backend systems portfolio project with reproducible tests, recorded failure evidence, and local benchmark results.

Key facts:

- Last reviewed: 2026-10-31. Responsive Vercel release preparation and private-token backend; current verification is in RELEASE-READINESS.md. Deployment and cloud availability are unclaimed.
- An acknowledged submission is saved only after its database transaction commits. Required idempotency keys deduplicate identical normalized requests and reject conflicting reuse.
- PostgreSQL is the durable authority. Claims use short transactions and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Workers execute task code outside database locks.
- A job is pending, running, succeeded, or failed. An expired attempt can lead to another attempt within the stored retry budget; expiry is not a separate job state.
- Each attempt has a worker identity, fencing token, and expiring lease. New heartbeats and outcomes require current unexpired ownership. An identical already-committed report can be acknowledged again without another transition.
- Task execution may repeat. Fencing protects executor state; external business effects require their own idempotency protection. Relevo does not claim exactly-once execution, guaranteed uptime, or recovery after database storage is destroyed.
- Built-in handlers hash a payload, wait for a configured duration, or deliberately fail a configured number of attempts. Report generation and other application workloads are integration examples, not implemented built-in handlers.
- Defaults include a 15-second lease, 5-second heartbeat interval, 2-second recovery scan interval, and three total attempts. These are configuration defaults, not recovery-time guarantees.
- The final backend code checkpoint 9af3ab8 passed 197 tests on Windows, Linux, a fresh checkout, and hosted CI. Treat these as dated verification results, not a live test counter.
- Retained benchmark experiments contain 1,440 measured jobs. The 50 ms worker monitor remains the default; optional 5 ms tuning helped some short-task cases and regressed timed workloads. Results describe the recorded revisions and local conditions, not a universal speedup or production capacity guarantee.
- The website demonstrates labeled playback of real recordings, independent of a running engine. Engine has illustrative Flow and recorded Replay tabs; Results presents retained measurements. Some business-effect recordings use explicit test lease expiry and instrumented transactions; interventions and untimed harness observations stay separate from committed transition events.

## Docs

- [Quickstart and local setup](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/README.md#running-and-testing): Prerequisites, local configuration, Docker Compose startup, tests, submission, and optional monitoring.
- [How the engine works](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/working.md): Plain-language architecture, job lifecycle, ownership, recovery, stored history, and limitations.
- [CLI and Python client guide](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/README.md#source-map): Client configuration, submit/inspect/attempts/wait operations, and an installed Compose demonstration.
- [HTTP API implementation](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/backend/src/relevo/api/app.py): The actual routes, authentication, health, metrics, and error handling.
- [Request and response contracts](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/backend/src/relevo/api/schemas.py): Source definitions for the public job operations and internal worker coordination messages.

## Evidence

- [Failure recordings and reproduction guide](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/artifacts/replays/README.md): What each recording demonstrates, source revisions, capture metadata, interventions, and reproduction commands.
- [Worker crash and recovery](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/artifacts/replays/worker-crash-recovery.json): Actual worker termination, lease expiry, replacement execution, and stale-report rejection.
- [Component restarts](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/artifacts/replays/component-restarts.json): Recorded API/database restarts and PostgreSQL process death with storage retained; acknowledged jobs remain accounted for.
- [Business-effect tests](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/backend/tests/integration/test_effects.py): Repeated execution creates duplicate unprotected effects; a stable business key protects the separate effect transaction.
- [Additional-expiry diagnostic](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/artifacts/replays/additional-expiry-diagnostic.json): A retained three-attempt run with one injected worker death. The additional expiry's cause is unassigned.
- [Clean-checkout verification](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/artifacts/verification/clean-checkout.json): Fresh credentials, Compose startup, CLI before/after restart, terminal-state preservation, and the complete backend suite.
- [Verified backend CI run](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/actions/runs/39067364211): Successful hosted verification for backend code checkpoint 9af3ab8.

## Results

- [Benchmark methodology](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md): Workloads, 1/3/5-worker cases, repetitions, hardware/configuration metadata, latency/resource observations, and raw-data links. The timed workload waits rather than performing CPU-heavy work; recorded finish timestamps precede commit acknowledgment.
- [Repeated comparison](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/benchmarks/comparison.md): Three repetitions per workload/worker group for the 50 ms baseline and optional 5 ms candidate.
- [Comparison limitations](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/benchmarks/experiment-notes.md): Confounders and reasons observed changes cannot all be attributed to the monitor interval.
- [Confirmation results](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/benchmarks/confirmation.md): Separate same-image confirmation with one repetition per group and visible timed-work regressions.
- [Confirmation limitations](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/benchmarks/confirmation-notes.md): Source-revision, logging, repeat-count, and interpretation limits.

## Project

- [Source repository](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo): Backend implementation, locked dependencies, tests, scripts, documentation, and recorded evidence.
- [Technical decisions](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/decision.md): Choices, alternatives, consequences, and verification, including PostgreSQL authority, fenced ownership, effect idempotency, and measured tuning.

## Optional

- [Test suite](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/tree/main/backend/tests): Unit and real-PostgreSQL integration tests, including concurrency, response loss, TCP faults, process crashes, and effect semantics.
- [Crash/recovery reproduction script](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/scripts/smoke_recovery.py): Deliberately stops/restarts local worker/scheduler services to verify bounded recovery and stale ownership rejection.
- [Benchmark harness](https://github.com/Tirthpanchori/Relevo/blob/main/scripts/benchmark.py): Runs isolated fixed workloads and validates acknowledged IDs, results, attempts, and history before retaining measurements.
